investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~143–148 s across all three checks before the eval runner timed out, producing empty evidence objects and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~143–148 s across all three checks before the eval runner timed out, producing empty evidence objects and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.rootCause: The snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was not refreshed within the required 300-minute window. The contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) asserts snapshotAgeMinutes max 300; the observed value was 332, a 32-minute overage. The snapshot source field reports "desktop-nightly-release" rather than "github-actions", indicating the last successful publish came from a desktop nightly release rather than the automated GitHub Actions workflow. No workflow-generated update arrived in time to satisfy the freshness contract. This is an eval-layer freshness failure; no evidence of a user-facing site outage is present.
